title: No source defines a configuration-version object or its operations, and the legacy key's panel is the partner panel
source: TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1, T3.2, appendix T-A; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.23; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14, 41, 43; Ownership Map v1
section: A2.23 Publish a panel change; T3.1; T3.2; T-A.1; RWB-P4-E8012-APP sections 1, 3, 4, 8, 11, 12.1, 12.2, 13; RWB-P4-E8012-CON sections 7 (AC1, AC2), 11, 12.1, 12.2, 13
description: The legacy story RWB-E8-012 publishes a partner panel change with an effective date and records it with the rule version. No source defines a configuration-version object, no endpoint inventory declares a publication or a list of configuration versions (T-A runs API-P4-004 to API-P4-021 only), and permission carries matrix_version and no date column, while masking_rule and delegation_limit carry valid_from and valid_to. The legacy panel is the partner panel, which the ownership map gives to S9 rwb-partner, so the target panel of this key is the access panel of P4. The effective-date bounds and the page bounds have no value in any source.
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T3.1: permission DF-REF-040 to DF-REF-044 with matrix_version and no date column; masking_rule DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-204; delegation_limit DF-REF-016 to DF-REF-026 and DF-REF-055 to DF-REF-062. T3.2 LOV-VERSION-STATUS. T-A.1 declares no configuration-version operation. FSD P4 v3 A2.23.1 says partner panel, A2.23.3.1 gives VR-P4-023-1 and BR-P4-023 only, and names no bound. Ownership Map v1 gives partner, partner_user and partner_instruction to S9.
owner_role: Solution architect, with the rwb-access tech lead and the rwb-case tech lead
proposed: Fix the two paths POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/config-versions/{versionId}/publish and GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/config-versions in RWB-P4-E8012-CON; treat a configuration version as the label triple of matrix_version, masking_version and limit_version over the three existing tables with no new table; hold the effective-date bounds and the page bounds as parameter rows of rwb-case read through DP-06; leave the partner panel and FEAT-PRM-02 to S9 rwb-partner.

title: The QA-sample operations, the missing P7 dependency, the draw rule and the reason-code set of RWB-E8-013 are not specified in any source
source: RWB-E8-013 legacy story; FSD P4 v3 A2.24; TSD P4 v3 T3.1, T4, T6.1, T6.3 and appendix T-A; Ownership Map v1; Architecture v5 slides 14, 41 and 44
description: The legacy story declares no endpoint of the QA sample, so the two operations this key needs (a write that runs the sample and a read that answers one run with its items), their request and answer fields, and the run state set are fixed by RWB-P4-E8013-CON and by no earlier document. The decision log and the rule registry are P7's (ownership rows decision_log_entry, rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case, ruling ASM-A6-tables-3), so the period read and the rule-model read are consumed through the P7 contract and its fake, yet the metadata of this key carries no P7 contract dependency: the dependency is declared in section 12.2 of both stories, built against the P7 fake, and raised here rather than added to the metadata. No source states how the sample is drawn, so the draw rule and the sample size are held as parameter rows of rwb-case read through DP-06. No source states what 'tests each against the rule version that was in force' means in the target; with no DP-04 in this key's pattern list the meaning taken is a time-travel consistency test over the recorded rule version, its valid_from and valid_to, its rule_row set and its action_text and outputs, and never a re-evaluation of a package. No source states the reason-code set, so PASS and FAIL and the codes RULE_VERSION_NOT_IN_FORCE, RULE_ROW_ABSENT and ANSWER_MISMATCH are held as parameter rows. The FSD P4 v3 screen list names SCR-39, SCR-40, SCR-41, SCR-42, SCR-43 and SCR-47 and no QA-sample screen, so the run is served as a panel of SCR-39 through the gateway-bff composite route and no screen id is invented.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E8-013 carries two acceptance criteria, a data table, two rule-version endpoints of the monolith, two screen names and four test cases and no operation of the sample; FSD P4 v3 A2.24 has one validation rule (VR-P4-024-1) and one business rule (BR-P4-024) and no field; TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A lists API-P4-004 to API-P4-021 and no sample operation; Ownership Map v1 puts decision_log_entry in P7 and the four rule tables in P7 under ASM-A6-tables-3; Architecture v5 slide 14 names the P7 reads GET /decisions?caseId= and GET /rule-models/{n}/{v}; FSD P4 v3 screens section lists no sample screen.
proposed: Freeze the two paths and the three schemas in RWB-P4-E8013-CON; add the P7 contract dependency to the metadata at the next revision rather than at build; fix the draw rule and the reason codes as parameter rows of rwb-case; confirm with the P7 owner that the rule-model read answers valid_from, valid_to and the rule_row set; record the sample as a panel of SCR-39 in RWB-PLT-N001-CON and raise a screen id only if the screen list is revised.
